newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS, ISLANDERS TIE ON GRAVES GARBAGE GOAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS, ISLANDERS TIE ON GRAVES GARBAGE GOAL.

text.p: Adam Graves scored a "garbage goal" late in the third period to lift the New York Rangers into a 1-1 tie with the New York Islanders Wednesday.

Goaltender Eric Fichaud held the Rangers scoreless for the first two periods, stopping all 13 shots. He was besieged by 14 shots in the third and the Rangers finally beat him with 2:33 left in the period.

Brian Leetch went the length of the ice and crossed into the Islanders' zone. He put a shot on goal from the left circle that Fichaud got a stick on, but the rebound came right to Graves, who flipped a shot over the goaltender's glove.
"Leetch just threw it on the net," Graves said. "We were lucky enough that it found an opening and went in."
"It was a fluke. Leetch was allowed to go coast-to-coast," Islanders coach Mike Milbury said. "He simply threw it out in front. It was a garbage goal. Nothing wrong with a garbage goal."
"I tried to cut the pass off," Fichaud said. "It went in off his stick or his pad. I don't know."
Each team had one shot in the overtime, with neither getting a quality scoring chance.
"They had a lot of shots in the third period. We did not want to take any chances, so we played it safe," said Fichaud.
Former Islander Glenn Healy made 21 saves for the Rangers, including several spectacular stops in the first period.
Ranger centre Wayne Gretzky was held pointless, ending his point-scoring streak at 15 games -- longest in the league this season and third longest in the Rangers' history.
Derek King tallied for the Islanders, who are 2-0-1 after a six-game winless streak.

In Anaheim, Martin Rucinsky recorded his second career hat trick and Vincent Damphousse added a goal and two assists as the Montreal Canadiens got their first road win of the season with a wild 6-5 victory over the Mighty Ducks.
Mark Recchi set up three goals and Saku Koivu had two assists for the Canadiens, who snapped a four-game winless streak. Montreal had been 0-5-1 in its first six road games.
Rookie Jose Theodore, making his third straight start, made 38 saves for his first NHL victory.
Paul Kariya scored his first two goals of the season and Kevin Todd had a goal and an assist for the Ducks, who are an NHL-worst 2-10-3.
In Phoenix, Mike Modano scored twice and Andy Moog made 29 saves to lead the Dallas Stars to a 3-2 win over the Coyotes.
Benoit Hogue also tallied for the Stars, who snapped a two-game losing streak and improved to 10-4.
Darrin Shannon and Dallas Drake had goals for the Coyotes, 2-2-1 in their last five games.
Moog has allowed just 19 goals in 11 games this season and leads the league with eight wins.
In San Jose, Keith Jones scored his first two goals in an Avalanche uniform and Patrick Roy came within 10:21 of his fourth shutout of the year as Colorado beat the Sharks, 4-1.
Jones came over from the Capitals Saturday for left wing Chris Simon and defenceman Curtis Leschyshyn.
Colorado is 4-0-3 in its last seven overall and has won four straight.
Roy, who leads all active goalies with 33 shutouts, lost his bid for number 34 when Al Iafrate scored at 9:39 of the third, his fourth goal in his last three games.
In Pittsburgh, Mario Lemieux and Glen Murray scored 10 seconds apart midway through the third period to lead the Penguins to a 5-2 victory over the Edmonton Oilers.
Pittsburgh has won two straight for the first time this season and has not lost to Edmonton at home since February 1993.
Jaromir Jagr scored his league-leading 11th goal for Pittsburgh in the first period.

At Detroit, John MacLean and Bobby Holik each scored a goal and Martin Brodeur recorded his 13th career shutout to lead the New Jersey Devils to a 2-0 victory over the Red Wings in the final meeting between the teams this season.
Valeri Zelepukin collected the assist on both scores for New Jersey (6-5-1), which entered the game with a league-low 25 goals.
In Hartford, Paul Ranheim and Geoff Sanderson each scored twice and Sean Burke recorded 27 saves as the Whalers snapped a five-game winless streak with a 5-1 victory over the Boston Bruins.
Jeff O'Neill had two assists for the Whalers, who had been 0-3-2 in their previous five games.
The Whalers were without Nelson Emerson, Gerald Diduck, Andrei Nikolishin and Glen Wesley, all suffering from the flu.
At Tampa Bay, Craig Berube's first goal of the season midway through the third period snapped a tie and lifted the Washington Capitals to a 2-1 win over the Lightning.
Brendan Witt scored the first goal for Washington. Rookie defenceman Drew Bannister tallied for Tampa Bay.
